sources.notes: §2.2.3 Vocalic inventories: the Northwest Caucasian vertical vowel system is "limited to two or three vocalic phonemes, commonly described as /ə/, /a/, and sometimes /aː/", and the two vowels are heavily coloured by adjacent consonants — anterior consonants give front vowels, rounded consonants rounded ones. Source for writing the two Abkhaz vowels /a/ and /ə/ and for treating surface [i e u o] as conditioned quality, not phonemes. §2.2.1 records that labialised alveolars are a prominent NWC feature and that Abkhaz realises them as doubly articulated stops. Retrieved from the author's preprint copy at https://gbegus.github.io/assets/pdf/BegusCaucasian.pdf.

sources.title: Abkhaz alphabet
sources.notes: READING PATH, not an authority: a letter-by-letter table of the modern Abkhaz Cyrillic alphabet, including the ⟨ь⟩/⟨ә⟩ palatalised and labialised digraphs. Used to enumerate which letters exist and which digraphs the orthography forms; every phonemic value the spec asserts is carried by begus2021, andersson2023 or hewitt1979.

notes: Abkhaz (аԥсшәа) — Northwest Caucasian, written since 1954 in an extended Cyrillic alphabet. INPUT CONTRACT: Cyrillic text in the modern (1954) Abkhaz orthography, Unicode NFC, lowercase folding applied by the engine. The orthography is heavily DIGRAPHIC: the modifier letters ⟨ь⟩ (palatalisation) and ⟨ә⟩ U+04D9 (labialisation) combine with a base consonant to spell a distinct phoneme (гь /ɡʲ/, гә /ɡʷ/, шь /ʃ/, шә /ʃʷ/, ҟә /qʷʼ/ …), so every such digraph is listed as its own grapheme key and is matched by maximal munch ahead of the bare letter. Only two vowels are phonemic, /a/ and /ə/ (begus2021 §2.2.3: the Northwest Caucasian vertical system is "commonly described as /ə/, /a/"; andersson2023 transcribes the language name /apʰsaʃʷa/). Their surface quality is coloured by the adjacent consonant rather than contrastive, so the [i e u o] qualities are allophonic; ⟨е о и у⟩ historically represent /aj aw jə wə/ sequences and are mapped to their surface values /e o i(j) u(w)/ as given in the alphabet table. ⟨ь⟩ and ⟨ә⟩ never occur alone as phonemes and are therefore not given standalone entries. The stops and affricates are a three-way voiced ~ aspirated ~ ejective series; the aspirated member carries ⟨ʰ⟩ throughout — ⟨ԥ⟩ /pʰ/, ⟨ҭ⟩ /tʰ/, ⟨ц⟩ /t͡sʰ/, ⟨ч⟩ /t͡ʃʰ/, ⟨ҽ⟩ /ʈ͡ʂʰ/ and ⟨қ⟩ /kʰ/, against ejective ⟨к⟩ /kʼ/ and voiced ⟨г⟩ /ɡ/. The 1996 orthographic reform replaced the hooked ⟨ҧ⟩ U+04A7, ⟨ҕ⟩ U+0495 and ⟨ӄ⟩ U+04C4 with the descender forms ⟨ԥ⟩ U+0525, ⟨ӷ⟩ U+04F7 and ⟨қ⟩ U+049A (⟨ҕь⟩ parallels modern ⟨ӷь⟩ /ʁʲ/); the hooked shapes are mapped so pre-reform text is not silently dropped. GOLD: the vox_communis ab row cannot score the language's central contrast and is documented, not chased. Measured over the cached TSV: of 76,464 word types, 44,279 (57.9%) carry the aligner's `spn` coverage marker instead of a transcription, and eight letters are at 100% `spn` — ⟨ә⟩ (30,743 types), ⟨ԥ⟩ (7,984), ⟨қ⟩ (7,058), ⟨ӡ⟩ (5,024), ⟨ҩ⟩ (4,035), ⟨ҿ⟩ (2,678), ⟨ӷ⟩ (1,741) and ⟨џ⟩ (811). ⟨ә⟩ is the labialisation modifier, so every labialised spelling is unscoreable, and the 32,185 scoreable types between them use only 35 distinct phone symbols, not one of which carries /ʷ/. Of the remaining distance, the largest parts are notation: normalising tie bars costs nothing, folding the gold's undotted ⟨ш ж ҽ ҿ⟩ series onto this spec's retroflex symbols removes 1.7 PER points, dropping aspiration the gold never writes removes 3.0, and reading ⟨е о и у⟩ as the gold's underlying /aj aw j w/ rather than surface /e o i u/ removes a further 8.3, leaving about 6.5 points of genuine disagreement out of a raw 45.2. The aspiration and the retroflex series are kept: andersson2023 writes /pʰ/ and hewitt1979 is the inventory authority, and the independent wikipron ab gold marks aspiration too.
